retell: Honey fakers cut their honey with cheap rice syrup and paid labs to tune their blends until they passed Europe's tests, until EU scientists brought in a sharper test that showed almost half the imports were suspected fakes, three times what anyone had caught before.
twist: The fakers weren't just cheating. They were paying labs to test their own fakes and tweak the syrup until it beat the official checks. Then the new test flipped it: one in seven turned out to be nearly one in two.
payoff: Yes. The title promises that the fakers were winning until Europe got smarter, and line 1 promises the real share was worse. Line 4 delivers the smarter test and line 5 gives the real number (almost half, three times the old count), so both promises are paid. The closing 'What's in your jar?' pulls it back to the viewer.
chain: Mostly yes. Line 2 sets up the motive (cheap syrup means profit). Line 3 follows with 'so': they tune blends to beat the tests. Line 4 turns with 'but': the sharper test catches the tuned blends. Line 5 follows with 'so': the real count comes out. Line 1 is a hook, not a link, and it gives the ending away early by saying 'the real share was worse', which takes some suspense out of line 5. No line is just 'and here is another fact'.
problems: Line 1's 'The real share was worse' gives away the ending in the first six seconds. Something like 'and the fakers were winning' would keep the suspense.
Line 2's 'about a quarter as much' is a fraction to work out at scroll speed. 'Dirt cheap' would land faster.
The ending tag 'What's in your jar?' is a stock line. Naming the threat to the viewer would hit harder, for example that the honey on their shelf might be one of the fakes.
